units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 57:3">Targ. Ps. LVII, 3</cite> <he>דְּיִגְמַר</he> (ed. Lag. <he>די גמר</he>, corr. acc.); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Pesachim 55a:15">Pes. 55ᵃ</cite> <he>גַּמְרִינָן</he> we dare finish a work commenced.
<cite ref="Pesachim 55a:15">Ib.</cite> <he>מִיגְמַר אין אתחולי לא</he> to finish is permitted, but not to begin; a. fr.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 1:16">Targ. Job I, 16</cite>.
Ib. XXII, 20; a. fr. (also Pa.).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 12:2">Targ. Ps. XII, 2</cite> <he>גְּמִירוּ</he> they are gone.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 5:11">Targ. Prov. V, 11</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Proverbs 22:8">Ib. XXII, 8</cite>; a. e.

<cite ref="Chullin 98b:8">Ḥull. 98ᵇ</cite> <he>ולִיגְמַר מיניה</he> now let one draw a conclusion from this (by analogy)! <cite ref="Chullin 98b:9">Ib.</cite> <he>מחידוש לא גַבְרִינָן</he> from an exception we draw no conclusions; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to be perfect, ready to answer, to know well. [Targ. Y. Deut. VI, 7 ותִגְמְרִינוּן וכ׳, read ותַגְ׳, v. infra.]—Part. גָּמֵיר.
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 63a:15">Sabb. 63ᵃ</cite> <he>והוה גְמִירְנָא וכ׳</he> and I knew well the whole Talmud (v. Rabh. D. S. a. l.).
Taan. 7ᵃ bot. דגְמִירֵי who are learned; ib. 7ᵇ top טפי הוו ג׳ they would be more learned; a. fr.—Whence: to learn by heart, esp. to learn traditional law (cmp. גְּרַס II).

<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 22:22">Targ. Job XXII, 22</cite> (h. text <cite ref="S00682"><he>קח</he></cite>, cmp. <cite ref="L00676"><he>לֶקַח</he></cite>).—Sabb. l. c. <he>לִיגְמַר איניש והדר ליסבר</he> one must first learn traditions, and then he may reason; <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 19a:19">Ab. Zar. 19ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="C01375"><he>גְּרַס</he> II</cite>.—
<cite ref="Berakhot 43a:1">Ber. 43ᵃ</cite> <he>וברכת … גַּמְרִינָן</he> and we are not sufficiently familiar with the laws concerning grace at meals.

<cite ref="Yoma 29a:2">Yoma 29ᵃ</cite> <he>מִיגְמַר בעתיקא וכ׳</he> to remember well something old (to refresh the memory) is more difficult than to commit to memory a fresh thing. Sabb. l. c. <he>למיגמר מיניה</he> from whom to receive traditions.
<cite ref="Sotah 36b:21">Sot. 36ᵇ</cite> <he>לא הוה קגמר</he> he could not remember; a. fr.—
Sabb. 96ᵇ גמרא גְמִירֵי לה they (the scholars) know it by tradition; ib. 97ᵃ הילכתא ג׳ לה.—גְּמִירֵי they have a tradition, it is a well-known maxim.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 37b:2">Snh. 37ᵇ</cite> bot.
<cite ref="Sotah 34a">Sot. 34ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Gittin 47a:8">Gitt. 47ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 21:13">Targ. Job XXI, 13</cite> ed. (Ms. <he>גַּמְרִין</he> Part. Pe.).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 13:28">Ib. XIII, 28</cite>; a. fr.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 6:7">Targ. Y. Deut. VI, 7</cite> [read:] <he>ותַגְמְרִינוּן</he> and thou shalt teach them (v.
<cite ref="Berakhot 13b">Ber. 13ᵇ</cite>).—
<cite ref="Sotah 36b:21">Sot. 36ᵇ</cite> <he>אַגְמְרֵיה ולא גמר</he> he taught him (the Hebrew language), but he (Pharaoh) could not remember it.
<cite ref="Chullin 45b:21">Ḥull. 45ᵇ</cite> <he>אַגְמְרָךְ גמרא</he> I will teach thee a tradition.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 17a:7">B. Kam. 17ᵃ</cite> <he>לאַגְמוּרֵי</he> as to teaching.
<cite ref="Berakhot 13b">Ber. 13ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="C01375"><he>גְּרַס</he> II</cite>.
